4 boneless, tied lamb sirloin rolls (about 2 pounds) or 8 double-thick lamb chops (about 6 pounds), trimmed of fat
1 teaspoon cornstarch mixed with 1 teaspoon cold water
1 tablespoon unsalted butter at room temperature (optional)
Kosher salt and freshly ground pepper
m: Stir the garlic, mint, ground coffee, ¼ cup oil and ⅓ cup wine together in a non-reactive bowl.
Grind the peppercorns, cumin, mustard and coriander seeds, rosemary and salt in a mortar or spice grinder and whisk into the coffee mixture.
Rub the marinade all over the lamb in a glass dish, cover and refrigerate 3 to 4 hours; wipe off most, but not all, of it with paper towels.
Cook the mushrooms and shallots in 2 tablespoons oil over medium heat 4 to 5 minutes, add the 1½ cups wine, vanilla bean and mint, boil, then simmer until reduced by half.
Stir in the stock, brewed coffee and honey and reduce by half again; remove the vanilla bean and thicken with the cornstarch slurry.
Off the heat swirl in the butter, season and keep warm.
Grill the lamb over a hot fire 7 to 8 minutes per side to medium-rare; plate with the sauce on top and mint sprigs.

i: 1 4- to 5-pound boned leg of veal, rolled and tied
½ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
1 red onion, peeled and thinly sliced
2 cups sliced portobello mushrooms, stems trimmed, inner gills removed
3 cups sliced shiitake mushrooms, stems trimmed
1 cup Pinot Noir or other red wine
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
GARNISH: chopped parsley, whole roasted shiitake mushrooms
m: Rub the veal with the paprika, salt and pepper; heat the oven to 325°F.
Cook the onion, mushrooms and herbs in the olive oil over medium heat 4 to 5 minutes until the onion is translucent, then spoon into a foil-lined roasting pan big enough for the veal.
Brown the roast lightly on all sides in the butter in the same pan and set it on the mushroom bed.
Pour over the wine and 1¼ cups stock and roast about 2 hours to an internal temperature of 170°F, basting occasionally.
Cut the string and tent the veal in foil; purée the mushroom mixture until smooth, thin with stock if you like, season and keep warm.
Slice the veal over a pool of mushroom sauce, scatter with walnuts, parsley and whole mushrooms; glazed dilled carrots and roasted potato quarters go well.

WLC|white bean soup with escargots and o.s: 6 to 8 as an appetizer or 4 as an entrée
i: 12 ounces white beans (such as Great Northern), rinsed and picked over
¾ cup cored, chopped fresh fennel
1 cup plum tomatoes, seeded and chopped
1 pound Yukon gold or new potatoes, diced
2 teaspoons chopped fresh rosemary (1 teaspoon dried)
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
¾ teaspoon chopped fresh rosemary (⅓ teaspoon dried)
m: Soak the beans overnight in cold water, then drain and discard any discoloured ones.
Sauté the carrot, celery, onions, fennel and garlic in 1½ tablespoons oil over medium heat 5 to 6 minutes in a large pot.
Add the beans, stock, tomatoes, potatoes, rosemary, mustard seed and fennel seed, boil, then cover and simmer 45 to 55 minutes until the beans are al dente; season.
Stir the olive paste, shallots, balsamic and rosemary together for the relish.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil, cook the garlic and escargots 3 to 4 minutes until warmed through, add the Pernod and cook 1 minute until it evaporates.
Ladle the soup into hot bowls, dollop relish on top, arrange the escargots around it and add rosemary sprigs.

i: 1 cup warm tap water (110° to 115°F on an instant-read thermometer)
¼ cup plus ½ tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil
2½ tablespoons chopped mixed herbs (parsley, basil, oregano)
2½ tablespoons chopped sun-dried tomatoes packed in oil
1 cup fresh or frozen okra, sliced in half lengthwise
3 tablespoons chopped fresh basil (1½ tablespoons dried)
1 tablespoon chopped fresh oregano (½ tablespoon dried)
12 ounces hot Italian, andouille, or chorizo sausage, cut into ¼-inch slices
1 cup grated Asiago or Parmesan cheese
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
m: Dissolve the sugar and yeast in the warm water and leave 8 to 10 minutes until foamy, then stir in ¼ cup oil for 15 to 20 seconds.
Pulse the flour, salt and pepper in a food processor, add the herbs and sun-dried tomatoes, then pour in the yeast mixture with the motor running until a ball forms, 30 to 45 seconds.
Knead on a floured surface 5 to 8 minutes until smooth and elastic, adjusting with warm water or flour as needed.
Turn the dough in a bowl coated with ½ tablespoon oil, cover with plastic and let rise in a warm spot about 1½ hours until doubled.
Sauté the okra, mushrooms, celery, carrots, onions, garlic, basil and oregano in 1 tablespoon oil over medium heat 7 to 8 minutes.
Brown the sausage slices in a non-stick pan 5 to 6 minutes and blot dry.
Whisk the tomato sauce, paste, filé and cayenne, then fold in the sausage, prosciutto, cheese and vegetables; season.
Heat the oven to 450°F. Punch down the dough, divide in four and roll into 8- to 9-inch rounds; brush with oil.
Fill one half of each round, fold over, roll and crimp the edges, press with a fork, brush with oil and prick the tops.
Bake on a cornmeal-dusted sheet on the top rack 16 to 18 minutes until golden, shielding the edges with foil if they darken; serve with basil leaves.

i: 1 tablespoon chopped fresh oregano (½ tablespoon dried)
1 tablespoon chopped fresh marjoram (½ tablespoon dried)
1 10-ounce package frozen chopped spinach, thawed and well drained
½ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
2 roasted yellow bell peppers (see page 116), peeled and seeded
¼ cup lightly toasted pine nuts
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
1 tablespoon chopped fresh oregano (½ tablespoon dried)
1 tablespoon chopped fresh basil (½ tablespoon dried)
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
m: Soften the onions and garlic in 1 tablespoon oil over medium heat 4 to 5 minutes, add the veal, oregano, marjoram, fennel seed and Worcestershire and cook 5 to 6 minutes until no longer pink; drain the fat.
Stir in the spinach and eggs for 2 to 3 minutes, then off the heat mix in the mozzarella, ricotta and bread crumbs; season with the salt, pepper, pepper flakes and cinnamon and cool.
Boil the manicotti 7 to 8 minutes (or per the package) until firm but cooked, hold in cold water, drain and pat dry.
Fill the tubes with the veal mixture, lay in an oiled baking dish and refrigerate.
Blend the roasted peppers, shallot, pine nuts and Worcestershire until smooth, stream in the oil, season and chill; bring to room temperature to serve.

For the sauce, cook the onions and garlic in ½ tablespoon oil 5 to 6 minutes, add the sherry, tomato sauce, tomatoes, paste, oregano, basil, sugar and pepper flakes and cook 7 to 8 minutes, stirring; season.
Pour the sauce over the manicotti, cover with foil and bake at 350°F for 30 minutes, then top with the grated mozzarella and bake uncovered 15 minutes more.
Serve two manicotti per plate with a dollop of pesto and a sprinkle of oregano.

i: ¾ tablespoon all-purpose flour plus more as needed
1 fennel bulb, cored and thinly sliced (about 2 cups)
1 tablespoon chopped fresh sage (½ tablespoon dried)
1 tablespoon chopped fresh rosemary (½ tablespoon dried)
½ cup pitted, chopped Kalamata olives
m: Rinse and dry the chicken, season with salt and pepper flakes and dust lightly with flour.
Brown the chicken on all sides in the butter and oil in a large stockpot over medium heat; drain on paper towels.
In the same pot sauté the garlic, onions, mushrooms, fennel, carrots, sage and rosemary 7 to 8 minutes.
Return the chicken with the stock, wine, tomatoes, tomato paste and olives, cover and simmer 50 to 55 minutes.
Lift out the chicken, reduce the sauce 15 minutes uncovered, then put the chicken back to heat through; season.
Serve in bowls with parsley and wedges of baked polenta topped with Parmesan.

i: ⅔ cup blood orange (or regular orange) juice
½ teaspoon blood orange (or regular orange) zest
⅛ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
1 teaspoon cornstarch mixed with 1 teaspoon cold water
1 tablespoon unsalted butter at room temperature (optional)
GARNISH: thin slices of blood orange
m: Whisk the marinade ingredients in a non-reactive bowl and pour over the tenderloins in a glass dish; refrigerate covered 3 to 4 hours, turning once.
Pat the pork dry, keep the marinade, and spread the mustard over the meat.
Simmer the marinade with the stock and cherries in a large pan about 15 minutes until it coats a wooden spoon.
Thicken slightly with the cornstarch slurry, whisk in the butter if using and keep warm.
Grill over hot coals 6 to 7 minutes, turn and cook 4 to 5 minutes more to medium-rare and juicy.
Slice, spoon over the sauce and garnish with blood orange slices.

i: ¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
2 spicy sausages (spicy Italian, andouille, or chorizo), cut in ½-inch slices
8 ounces mussels, debearded and rinsed (see page 58)
1 large roasted red pepper, diced (see page 116)
¾ cup fresh or defrosted frozen peas
m: Rinse and dry the thighs, rub with ¼ teaspoon salt and the pepper and rest a few minutes.
Brown the chicken on both sides in ½ tablespoon oil in a non-stick pan; drain on paper towels.

In a paella pan fry the sausage and escargots in the remaining 2 tablespoons oil 3 to 4 minutes, add the garlic and onions for 3 minutes, then the rice, remaining ¼ teaspoon salt, saffron, paprika and turmeric and stir 5 minutes to coat.
Add the wine and let it evaporate, then the stock; bring to a boil and drop to a simmer.
Nestle the chicken and mussels over the rice, cover and cook 17 to 18 minutes until the chicken is done and the rice al dente.
Scatter the roasted pepper, parsley and peas on top, cover 2 to 3 minutes just to warm, keeping the peas bright; season.
Finish with more parsley and serve from the pan, one thigh each with the mussels and escargots shared out.

WLC|basil fettuccine with sun-dried toma.s: 5 to 6 as an appetizer or 2 to 4 as an entrée
i: 1¼ cups sliced crimini or shiitake mushrooms
¾ cup Zinfandel or other red wine
1 cup julienned sun-dried tomatoes packed in oil
⅔ cup pitted, chopped Kalamata olives
3 tablespoons chopped fresh basil (1½ tablespoons dried)
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
1¼ pounds fresh or dried basil fettuccine noodles
½ cup freshly grated Parmesan cheese
m: Cook the garlic, onions and mushrooms in the oil over medium heat 3 to 4 minutes until the onions are translucent.
Add the wine, sun-dried tomatoes, tomato paste, tomato sauce, olives, basil, fennel seed and balsamic and simmer, stirring, about 8 minutes until slightly thickened.
Keep warm over low heat, loosening with more wine if it gets too thick; season lightly, remembering the prosciutto is salty.
Cook the fettuccine in salted boiling water 3 to 5 minutes until al dente, drain and return to the pot over medium heat.
Divide the noodles between plates, spoon over the sauce and top with Parmesan, prosciutto and walnuts; scatter with basil and serve at once.

i: 1 teaspoon fines herbes (see page 36) or dried oregano
m: Slice the eggplants lengthwise ¼ inch thick, salt with 1 teaspoon and leave on paper towels 30 minutes; rinse, dry and roast on an oiled sheet at 375°F for 30 minutes.
Brown the lamb with the onions and garlic over medium-high heat, crumbling it; drain in a strainer and blot on paper towels.
Return the meat to the cleaned pan with the remaining salt, pepper, nutmeg, cinnamon, fines herbes, parsley and tomato paste; add the wine and simmer 10 minutes.
Grease a 9-by-13-inch dish and dust with the bread crumbs, holding back 3 tablespoons.
For the sauce, melt the butter, whisk in the flour, then stir in the milk, nutmeg and salt until thick.
Temper the egg yolk with a little hot sauce, add the reserved crumbs, and blend back into the sauce.
Layer eggplant, meat and plenty of feta; repeat, then top with the sauce.
Sprinkle with Parmesan and bake at 350°F for 50 to 60 minutes until golden. Cut in squares and garnish with parsley.

i: 4½ pounds chicken breasts, thighs, and legs
⅓ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
½ cup pitted, sliced Spanish green olives
1 tablespoon cornstarch mixed with 1 tablespoon cold water
m: Rinse and dry the chicken and dust all over with the salt, pepper and 2 tablespoons of the flour.
Cook the pancetta in the butter in a large pot over medium heat 5 to 6 minutes, then brown the chicken in batches about 5 minutes a side; set on paper towels.
Brown the remaining tablespoon of flour in the pot 1 to 2 minutes, then cook the onions, mushrooms, garlic and herbs 5 minutes.
Add the wine, tomatoes, tomato paste, stock and chicken; boil, then cover and simmer 30 minutes.
Add the pearl onions and olives and cook 10 minutes more. Lift out the chicken and keep warm under foil.
Stir the cornstarch slurry and mustard into the liquid and boil hard 6 to 7 minutes to thicken; season.
Serve the chicken in bowls with plenty of sauce and parsley, with rice or pasta and garlic bread.

i: ½ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
2 pounds cubed pork stew meat (from the shoulder or roast)
2 stalks celery, ends trimmed and diced
1 large red bell pepper, cored, seeded, and chopped
2 tablespoons chopped fresh oregano (1 tablespoon dried)
12 ounces tomatillos, husked, rinsed, and cut into quarters
1 roasted red pepper, seeded and chopped (see page 116)
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
m: Soak the beans 8 hours or overnight (or boil and stand 1 hour in the hot water); drain, rinse and pick over.
Toss the pork in the chili powder, cumin, cayenne, achiote, basil, pepper and salt.
Cook the pancetta in a heavy pot until barely browned; remove it and pour off the fat.
Heat the oil and sauté the pork, garlic, onion, celery, red pepper, jalapeños and oregano 7 to 8 minutes until the pork colours.
Return the pancetta and add the wine, stock, beans, cilantro, bay leaf and cloves; boil, then cover and simmer 1 hour.
For the salsa, sauté the tomatillos, onion, shallot, garlic, jalapeño, roasted pepper and cumin in the oil 10 to 12 minutes until softening; cool, then stir in the cilantro and season.
Ladle the stew into bowls, top with salsa and a dollop of sour cream, and add cilantro sprigs; serve with garlic bread or corn tortillas.

i: 1½ tablespoons chopped fresh oregano (¾ tablespoon dried)
⅛ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
½ leg of lamb, boned, butterflied, and trimmed of most fat (about 2 pounds meat)
1 large whole head of garlic, unpeeled
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
m: Mix the marinade, seal it with the lamb in a plastic bag and refrigerate at least 2 to 3 hours, turning now and then. Pat the lamb dry.
Trim the tip off the garlic head, drizzle with the oil, season, wrap loosely in foil and roast at 350°F for 45 to 50 minutes; squeeze out the cloves.
For the sauce, soften the shallots in the oil 2 to 3 minutes, add the wine and reduce by half.
Add the stock, mint, roasted garlic and mustard and reduce by half again; season.
Grill the lamb over a hot fire 8 to 9 minutes a side for medium-rare, taking the thin end pieces off first.
Slice, spoon over the sauce and scatter with mint.

i: ⅛ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
1 rehydrated dried chipotle pepper, stemmed and minced, or ¼ teaspoon chipotle chiles in adobo (see page 175)
4 ears fresh (or frozen) corn, husks removed
½ cup chopped roasted red bell pepper (see page 116)
2 tablespoons chopped fresh basil (1 tablespoon dried)
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
m: Whisk the marinade, bag it with the steak and refrigerate 4 to 5 hours, turning occasionally; drain, keeping the marinade for basting.
Rub the corn with olive oil and roast at 350°F for 45 minutes, then cut off the kernels (about 2 cups).
Cook the pancetta over low-medium heat 8 to 10 minutes until lightly browned; drain and blot.
Mix the corn with the pancetta, bell pepper, garlic, Worcestershire, jalapeños, vinegar and basil; season and chill, then bring to room temperature.
Grill the steak over a hot fire 5 minutes a side for rare, rest 5 minutes under foil and slice thinly against the grain on an angle.
Spoon salsa onto each plate and top with slices of steak.

i: 12 ounces Italian sausage, cut into ½-inch slices
¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper or red pepper flakes
1 pound dried penne or other small dried pasta
GARNISH: shredded Asiago cheese, chopped parsley
m: Soak the porcini in hot water 2 to 3 hours and drain.
Brown the sausage slices in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat 6 to 7 minutes; blot on paper towels.
In a large pan cook the onions and garlic 4 to 5 minutes until translucent, then add both mushrooms, the herbs, salt and pepper for 3 to 4 minutes.
Pour in the Syrah, boil, then simmer until reduced by half.
Add the tomatoes and tomato paste and simmer 8 to 10 minutes; return the sausage to heat through and season.
Boil the penne in salted water until al dente, drain, and toss with the sauce in the pot, reheating if needed.
Serve in four bowls topped with Asiago and parsley.

i: ¼ teaspoon fresh ground black pepper
1 6- to 7-pound whole leg of lamb, boned, butterflied, and trimmed of excess fat (about 4½ pounds meat)
1 tablespoon chopped fresh rosemary (½ tablespoon dried)
¼ cup pitted, sliced green olives
¼ cup pitted and sliced Kalamata olives
m: Whisk the marinade ingredients in a non-reactive bowl, pour into a large sealable bag with the lamb and marinate 4 to 6 hours, turning occasionally.
Sauté the shallots and mushrooms in the olive oil over medium heat 3 to 4 minutes, add the wine and boil down by half.
Add the stock and rosemary and reduce by half again.
Stir in the mustard and olives and simmer gently until the sauce coats a wooden spoon; keep warm.
Pat the lamb dry, keeping the marinade for basting, and grill over very hot coals 7 to 8 minutes a side to medium-rare, basting now and then; take the thin ends off early.
Rest under foil a few minutes, slice thinly and serve on warm plates with the sauce and rosemary sprigs; roasted potato quarters and tomatoes gratinée go well.

i: ¾ tablespoon whole mixed peppercorns, lightly crushed
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
m: Oil the filets, press the crushed peppercorns and salt onto the tops and sides, and spread the tops with mustard.
Soften the garlic in the butter over low-medium heat 3 to 4 minutes.
Add the wine, vinegar, mustard, Worcestershire, stock, Cognac and tomato paste; boil, then simmer until reduced by half.
Add the cream and reduce a little more to thicken; season and adjust the consistency.
Grill the filets over very hot coals 8 to 10 minutes, turn and give them 5 to 6 minutes more for rare, or longer to taste.
Pool the sauce on the plates and set the filets on top; asparagus and sweet potato purée suit it.

i: ½ teaspoon coriander seed, toasted and crushed
1½ tablespoons chopped, seeded pasilla chiles (see NOTE)
1 tablespoon chopped chipotle chiles in adobo (see NOTE)
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
8 ounces feta cheese (tomato-basil, if available), cut into ¼-inch cubes
1 cup chopped, roasted, peeled, and seeded peppers (yellow and red bell peppers, Anaheim chiles)
m: Rub the pork all over with the salt, pepper, cinnamon, cumin, oregano and sage.
Brown it on all sides and both ends in the olive oil over medium heat; move to a baking dish and keep the oil in the pan.
Roast at 350°F about 1½ hours to an internal temperature of 165°F (indirect medium heat on a gas grill also works).
For the mole, cook the onions and garlic in the reserved pan 5 to 6 minutes, add the sesame seeds, spices, chiles and cilantro for 3 to 4 minutes, then add the stock and simmer 10 minutes.
Blend the mixture with the peanut butter, tomato paste, raisins, chocolate and lime juice until smooth; return to the pan and simmer covered 35 to 40 minutes, thinning with stock if needed. Season.
For the rice, sweat the shallots and onions in the butter and oil 4 to 5 minutes, then toast the rice, cumin, oregano and fennel seed 2 to 3 minutes.
Add the stock and tomatoes, boil, then simmer covered 10 to 12 minutes until nearly dry; stir in the feta and peppers, cover 5 to 7 minutes more, rest 10 minutes and fluff.
Slice the pork, spoon over the mole, serve the rice alongside and garnish with cilantro and lime.

i: 3 red bell peppers, halved and seeded
½ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
⅛ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
1 teaspoon chopped fresh basil (½ teaspoon dried)
1 teaspoon chopped fresh oregano (½ teaspoon dried)
GARNISH: basil leaves, grated Parmesan cheese
m: Smoke the tomatoes, onions, peppers and shallots on foil-lined racks over wet fruitwood, oak or hickory chips for 2 to 3 hours, topping up the chips as needed.
Peel, seed, drain and chop the tomatoes; peel and chop the onions and shallots; seed and chop the peppers.

Sweat the onions, peppers, shallots and herbs in the oil 8 to 10 minutes, add the tomatoes, sherry, vinegar, tomato paste and roasted garlic and simmer uncovered 15 minutes; add the salt, pepper and pepper flakes.
Purée in batches about 45 seconds until smooth; keep 2 cups for the dish and freeze the rest.
Trim the duck breasts, cut small X slashes in the fat, and marinate skin side down with the oil, Worcestershire, hot sauce, salt, pepper, basil and oregano for 3 to 4 hours in the fridge.
Sear skin side down over medium-high heat 5 to 6 minutes, turn and cook 3 to 4 minutes to medium-rare.
Rest briefly, slice at an angle, top with the sauce and finish with basil leaves and Parmesan; garlicky sautéed spinach alongside.

i: ½ teaspoon toasted mustard seed, crushed
1 teaspoon chopped fresh thyme (½ teaspoon dried)
¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
1 teaspoon cornstarch mixed with 1 teaspoon cold water
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
m: Whisk the marinade, seal with the tenderloins in a plastic bag and refrigerate 3 to 4 hours; pat the pork dry and keep the marinade.
Oil the washed beets and roast at 350°F for 55 to 60 minutes until the skins shrivel; cool, peel and cut into ¼-inch dice.
Boil the marinade (minus the bay leaf) and simmer until reduced by half.
Add the cranberry juice, stock, vinegar and beets and reduce by half again, then add the cornstarch slurry and cook until thickened.
Off the heat swirl in the butter if using, season and keep warm.
Grill the pork over a hot fire 8 to 9 minutes, turn and cook 5 to 6 minutes more until medium-rare; rest in foil.
Spoon the sauce onto plates and set sliced pork on top with parsley; horseradish mashed potatoes alongside.

i: 1 tablespoon chopped fresh tarragon leaves (½ tablespoon dried)
⅛ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
4 green onions, ends trimmed and minced
1 tablespoon chopped fresh tarragon (1½ teaspoons dried)
⅛ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
1 cup pitted and halved fresh cherries
m: Whisk the marinade in a non-reactive bowl, pour into a sealable bag with the venison and refrigerate 3 to 4 hours.
Boil the chow mein noodles in salted water 1½ minutes, stirring to separate; drain, cool in cold water and drain again.
Toss the noodles with the green onions, corn, tarragon, zest, olive oil, salt and pepper.
Press the mixture into a 12-inch non-stick pan of hot vegetable oil over medium heat and cook 6 to 7 minutes, flip, and cook 5 to 6 minutes more until golden and crisp; drain, quarter and keep warm.
Pat the venison dry and put the marinade in a pan with the stock and cherries; boil, then simmer until halved and coating a spoon.
Stir in the port and mustard and simmer 5 minutes more to thicken; season and swirl in the butter off the heat.
Grill the venison over red-hot coals 3 to 4 minutes a side, no more than medium-rare, slice thinly and serve with the sauce and noodle cake.

i: ⅛ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
2 cups peeled and diced celery root
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
½ cup shredded smoked mozzarella cheese
m: Cut the veal into 1-inch cubes and dust with the flour, salt and pepper.
Brown the veal with the pancetta in the butter over medium heat 6 to 7 minutes.
Add the mushrooms, celery root, onions, garlic, paprika, caraway and fines herbes and cook 8 minutes more.
Pour in the stock and wine, boil, then cover and simmer 1¼ hours; season.
Serve piping hot, topped with the pecans and smoked mozzarella, with wild rice and sautéed spinach.

i: 1 tablespoon chopped fresh rosemary (½ tablespoon dried)
8 ounces Gorgonzola cheese, cut into small chunks
¼ cup lightly toasted walnut halves
¾ tablespoon chopped roasted garlic (see page 164)
2 tablespoons herb-flavored (basil or oregano) or extra-virgin olive oil
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
m: Whisk the oil, garlic, vinegar, rosemary, salt and pepper over the steaks in a glass dish and refrigerate covered 2 to 3 hours.
Process all the “butter” ingredients about a minute until well mixed; serve at room temperature.
Pour boiling stock over the bulgur, cover with foil and stand about 30 minutes until absorbed.
Stir the tomatoes, mint, chives, roasted garlic, green onions, paprika and oil into the bulgur and season.
Grill the steaks over a hot fire 5 to 6 minutes a side or to taste; soon after turning, mound some Gorgonzola butter on each to half-melt.
Serve with the tabbouleh and a dish of extra butter at the table.

i: 2 medium globe eggplants, cut horizontally in ½-inch slices
2 tablespoons chopped fresh oregano (1 tablespoon dried)
½ teaspoon fennel seed, toasted and crushed
m: Whisk the marinade, spoon it over the filets and refrigerate covered 2 to 3 hours.
Rub the eggplant slices with 1 tablespoon of the oil, salt them and roast at 350°F for 40 minutes; chop into ½-inch cubes.
Cook the onions in the remaining 1½ tablespoons oil over medium-high heat 3 to 5 minutes until translucent.
Add the tomatoes, roasted garlic, herbs, fennel seed and eggplant and cook 8 to 10 minutes, stirring; season and keep warm.
Grill the filets over very hot coals 5 to 7 minutes a side for medium-rare or to taste.
Spoon the ragout onto plates with the filets beside it.

i: 2 tablespoons chopped fresh basil (1 tablespoon dried)
¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
1½ cups sliced crimini or shiitake mushrooms
½ cup red wine (preferably Cabernet Sauvignon)
¼ ounce dried morel or porcini mushrooms (rehydrated in cold water, drained, and halved)
2 tablespoons chopped fresh basil (1 tablespoon dried)
½ teaspoon cornstarch mixed with ½ teaspoon cold water
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
m: Whisk the marinade in a non-reactive bowl, pour over the chops in a glass dish and refrigerate covered 3 to 4 hours; pat dry.
Cook the shallots and crimini in the oil over medium heat 3 to 4 minutes until the shallots turn golden.
Add the green peppercorns, vinegar and wine and simmer until reduced by half.
Add the stock and morels and reduce by half again.
Stir in the basil, mustard and cornstarch slurry to thicken until the sauce coats a spoon; season.
Grill the chops over hot coals 8 to 10 minutes, turn and cook 7 to 8 minutes more for medium-rare or to taste.
Top the chops with the sauce and chopped basil; sautéed fresh peas go alongside.

i: 1 tablespoon chopped fresh rosemary (½ tablespoon dried, crushed)
¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
½ leg of lamb, butterflied and trimmed of excess fat (about 2 pounds net)
2 tablespoons chopped fresh basil (1 tablespoon dried)
1 cup seeded, chopped fresh plum tomatoes
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
m: Whisk the marinade, pour into a sealable bag with the lamb and refrigerate 2 to 3 hours; pat the lamb dry.
Soak the porcini in very hot water 45 minutes until soft, squeeze out the water and cut each into thirds.
Fry the pancetta in the oil over medium heat 4 to 5 minutes, then add the onions, roasted garlic and basil and cook 6 to 7 minutes until translucent.
Add the wine and porcini and simmer 10 minutes to reduce by half.
Add the stock, mustard and tomatoes and simmer 15 minutes until the sauce coats a spoon; season.
Grill the lamb over hot coals 8 to 9 minutes, turn and grill 7 to 8 minutes more until medium-rare; slice thinly.
Pool the sauce on plates, lay the lamb on top and sprinkle with parsley; serve with polenta cakes and winter squash.

i: 1 tablespoon chopped fresh sage (½ tablespoon dried)
¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
1 tablespoon chopped fresh sage (½ tablespoon dried)
⅛ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
1 tablespoon port or crème de cassis
2 tablespoons unsalted butter at room temperature
m: Combine the marinade in a sealable bag with the venison and refrigerate 3 to 4 hours or overnight; pat dry and keep the marinade.
Whiz the bread in a food processor about 1 minute, then add the shallots, sage, salt, pepper, mustard and oil for 20 to 30 seconds more.
Press the coating onto the top and sides of the venison and set it on a broiler pan.
Reduce the reserved marinade and wine by half in a large pan.

Add the stock, currants, port and mustard and reduce by half again until the sauce coats a spoon; strain, whisk in the butter and keep warm, adding a dash of balsamic if it tastes too sweet against the wine.
Broil the venison 7 to 8 minutes until rare; do not overcook.
Slice and serve with the currant sauce; corn fritters and sugar snap peas suit it.

i: 1 4½-pound prime rib roast of beef (2 ribs), trimmed and tied
½ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
2 teaspoons minced fresh rosemary (1 teaspoon dried)
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
½ teaspoon cornstarch mixed with ½ teaspoon cold water
m: Set the roast fat side up on a rack in a flameproof roasting pan and coat it with ½ tablespoon mustard, ½ teaspoon horseradish, ¾ tablespoon rosemary, the salt and pepper; roast at 450°F for 20 minutes.
Toss the onion, shallot, carrots, celery and mushrooms with a little olive oil, salt and pepper in a baking dish; lower the oven to 350°F and roast the vegetables on a rack below the beef for 1 hour.
Blend the flour, eggs, milk, chives, rosemary and salt until smooth and chill covered at least 45 minutes.
Take out the vegetables and chop roughly; give the roast 10 minutes more to rare or medium-rare, then rest it under foil 20 to 30 minutes. Keep the pan unwashed.
Heat the oven to 425°F, melt the butter and oil in a shallow dish 3 to 4 minutes, pour in the chilled batter and bake 18 to 20 minutes until risen and golden; cut in four.
Deglaze the roasting pan with the Cabernet over medium heat, scraping, 6 to 7 minutes until halved.
Add the stock, the remaining ½ tablespoon mustard, ½ teaspoon horseradish and 1 tablespoon rosemary, and the vegetables; reduce by half, thicken with the cornstarch slurry and season.
Carve into four portions, spoon over the jus, sprinkle with chives and serve the pudding alongside.

i: ¼ pound (1 stick) cold unsalted butter, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 cup cold water plus more as needed for filling
GARNISH: crème fraîche or whipped cream, mint sprigs
m: Pulse the flour, sugar and cinnamon with the butter to coarse pea-sized meal, add the salt dissolved in the water and blend just until the dough comes together.
Roll to an 11-inch circle ⅛ inch thick, fit into a 10-inch removable-bottom tart pan and chill 15 minutes.
Prick the shell, line with foil, fill with weights and bake at 400°F on a sheet 15 to 20 minutes until light golden; remove the foil and weights and cool fully.
Simmer the apricots, peaches, port and 1 cup water 8 to 10 minutes until soft; strain, keeping the fruit, and top the liquid up with cold water to 1 cup.
Whisk ¼ cup of the liquid with the brown sugar and cornstarch; return the rest to the pot with the slurry and orange juice.
Boil, stirring, then simmer until thickened; stir in the fruit and pecans, cool completely and pour into the shell.
Unmould onto a plate and serve chilled or at room temperature with crème fraîche and mint.

i: ¼ pound (1 stick) cold unsalted butter, cut into 1-inch pieces
6 cups peeled, sliced green apples (about 4 to 5 medium apples)
2 tablespoons all-purpose flour, tapioca flour, or instant tapioca
GARNISH: small wedges of Stilton cheese
m: Pulse the flour, sugar and cinnamon with the butter to coarse pea-sized meal, add the salt dissolved in the water and blend just until the dough gathers.
Roll to an 11-inch circle ⅛ inch thick, fit into a 9-inch pie pan, trim the overhang and chill 15 minutes.
Gently toss all the filling ingredients together in a large bowl.
Fork together the flour, brown sugar and crystallized ginger, then rub in the butter until no lumps show.
Fill the shell, scatter over the streusel and crimp the edge.
Bake on a sheet in the middle of a 375°F oven about 1 hour until golden and bubbling, shielding the rim with foil from 35 to 40 minutes in until 55 minutes.
Cool and serve each slice with a small wedge of Stilton.

i: ½ pound (2 sticks) cold unsalted butter, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 tablespoon fresh lemon or lime juice
m: Pulse the flour, sugar and cinnamon with the butter to coarse pea-sized meal, add the salt dissolved in the water and blend just until it comes together; divide into two balls.
Wrap one round and chill it for the lattice; roll the other to an 11-inch circle ⅛ inch thick, line a 9-inch pie pan and refrigerate.
Mix the apricots and berries with the sugar, cornstarch, lemon juice, cinnamon and cardamom and stand at least 15 minutes.
Pour the filling into the shell.
Roll the second round to 11 inches, cut 8 to 10 strips ½ inch wide, weave them crisscross on top, pinch the ends into the base and flute or fork the edge.
Wrap the rim in a 2- to 3-inch band of foil and bake in the middle of a 425°F oven 55 to 60 minutes until golden and bubbling, removing the foil 15 to 20 minutes before the end.

i: 2 tablespoons cold unsalted butter, cut into bits
m: Heat the oven to 400°F and lay the figs cut side up in a buttered 8-by-8-by-2-inch dish with the raspberries scattered over.
Grind the almonds finely with the flour in a blender or processor.
Add ⅓ cup sugar, the eggs, milk and port and blend smooth, scraping down the sides.
Pour the batter over the fruit, dot with the butter and sprinkle with the remaining 2 tablespoons sugar.
Bake in the middle of the oven 30 to 40 minutes until golden and set; cool 20 minutes and dust with powdered sugar.

i: ¼ cup quick-cooking tapioca or tapioca flour
½ cup (1 stick) unsalted butter or margarine
m: Mix the sugar, tapioca, cinnamon and orange peel in a shallow 2-quart baking dish.
Add the rhubarb, berries and lime juice, toss well and stand at least 30 minutes, stirring a few times to soften the tapioca.
Blend the flour, butter, brown sugar and nutmeg until lumpy and crumble evenly over the fruit.
Bake in the middle of a 375°F oven about 35 minutes until golden and bubbling.
Cool on a rack 15 to 20 minutes and serve, with lemon sorbet if you like.

i: 5 ounces (10 tablespoons) unsalted butter at room temperature
1 pound brioche, challah, or egg bread, cut into ½-inch-thick slices
2 pounds fresh peaches, poached, skinned, pitted, and sliced or one 29-ounce can, drained
m: Heat the oven to 275°F; butter the bread lightly on both sides and toast it in the oven.
Purée half the peaches, keep half the purée for garnish, and mix the rest with the sliced peaches and bananas.
Whisk the eggs, then ¾ cup of the sugar and the milk, hard for 2 minutes; stir in the fruit.
Butter a 3-inch-deep loaf pan generously and dust with 2 tablespoons of the remaining sugar.
Layer bread and fruit custard alternately until ½ inch from the top; stand 1 hour.
Mix the cinnamon into the last of the sugar, sprinkle over, cover with foil and bake 1 hour 15 minutes.
Rest 2 hours at room temperature and serve with mint sprigs and the reserved purée.
